questions.question: Where does the causal graph get built, given the normalizer drops tool_result records and breaks the parentUuid spine?

options.label: Fix normalizer, build on events (Recommended)
options.description: Add a lightweight tool_result stub event (uuid, parentUuid, tool_use_id, is_error, timestamp — no content) so the spine is intact and privacy-safe. Graph is built from normalized events, works identically for local and server-side consumers.

options.label: Build inside the normalizer
options.description: Normalizer emits a `graph` section alongside `events`, using raw JSONL while both call and result are in scope. No schema change to events, but graph logic is coupled to the collector and can't be recomputed server-side.

options.label: Separate builder over raw JSONL
options.description: New module parses ~/.claude/projects JSONL independently for full fidelity. Duplicates normalizer work and means graph construction touches unredacted file content.

questions.question: What is v1 scope for the graph — how much of the OTEL overlay is in?

options.label: JSONL spine only (Recommended)
options.description: Ship structure, tokens (deduped by message.id), turns, subagent links, skill attribution. No OTEL join. The corpus shows JSONL alone answers 6 of your 7 questions; OTEL only sharpens token accuracy and adds rejected-call nodes.

options.label: JSONL spine + OTEL overlay together
options.description: Build the join on request_id / tool_use_id in v1. Higher fidelity tokens and permission-decision nodes, but doubles the surface and needs the collector config wired first.

options.label: Design both, implement spine first
options.description: Design doc specifies the full overlay contract and join keys; implementation plan phases OTEL into a later milestone.

questions.question: How should the graph be persisted / consumed?

options.label: JSON artifact + in-memory API
options.description: Serialized node/edge JSON per session (ids only, on-disk form), plus a Python loader that resolves ids to object pointers — matches the 'ids on disk, pointers in memory' split in your notes.

options.label: Query-first — build for the 7 questions
options.description: Design the analytics queries (loops, budget hotspots, cache behavior, waste, subagent ROI) first and let those dictate the graph shape and any indices.

options.label: Both — artifact is the substrate, queries layer on top
options.description: Define the graph artifact as the stable contract, then specify the 7 questions as query functions over it. More design work up front.

# Normalizer fix: restore the dropped `tool_result` record

## Context

We are designing a causal graph over Claude Code sessions (`docs/design/notes/Causal-trace-graph-notes.md`).
Analysis of the raw corpus at `/Users/sumandra/projects/talium/traces/` showed the graph cannot be
built on normalized output today, because the normalizer discards every `tool_result` record.

`src/collector/normalizer/claude_code.py:242-268` (`_handle_user`) merges result-derived fields into
the open `tool_call` payload and then `return`s **without emitting an event**. The record is gone.
A TODO at line 254-261 flags this, but understates it as a loss of "rich `toolUseResult` fields" —
what is actually lost is the whole record envelope.

Measured across the corpus (9 sessions, 4,133 top-level records, 120 subagent streams):

- **4,996 `tool_result` records dropped.**
- **16% of assistant events have a dangling `parent_id`** (131 of 805 in one session) — their
  `parentUuid` points at a dropped `tool_result`, so the `uuid`/`parentUuid` spine is broken.
- **`sourceToolAssistantUUID` lost — present on 4,996/4,996 (100%)** of these records. It is the
  direct result→call edge; today it never reaches a consumer.
- **`promptId` lost on 4,992/4,996.** This is the native turn key. Losing it on tool_results breaks
  positional carry-forward, which is how assistant records get their turn attribution.
- **40 `toolDenialKind` values lost** (`permission-rule` 29, `user-rejected` 7,
  `automode-unavailable` 2, `interrupted` 2) — every rejected/blocked tool call in the corpus.
- **Subagent outcomes lost.** `_handle_spawn` (line 314) never registers in `open_tool_calls`, so the
  Task `tool_result` has no merge target and is dropped with nothing extracted. Its `toolUseResult`
  carries `status`, `agentId`, `resolvedModel` (120 occurrences).

The sensitive payload is confined to two places and must stay out: `toolUseResult.*` (stdout, stderr,
originalFile, oldString/newString, content, file) and the `tool_result` block's `content` body.
Everything else on the record is metadata.

**Outcome:** the `tool_result` record ships as its own event with tool output stripped, the parent
chain resolves end-to-end, and the graph work can proceed against verified normalized output.

Scope is the normalizer fix only. Turn segmentation, the graph model, and the design document are
deliberately out of scope and come next.

## Changes

### 1. `src/collector/normalizer/claude_code.py` — emit the event

**`_handle_user`** (line 242): where it currently returns after `_merge_tool_result`, emit one
`tool_result` event per `tool_result` block. The existing enrich-in-place merge into `tool_call` is
unchanged — this is purely additive. Delete the TODO at 254-261.

New builder `_make_tool_result(record, block, raw_record) -> EventIn`:

```
event_type: "tool_result"
record_id:  record["uuid"]          # the result record's own uuid — Tier 1, per the
                                    # record_id-tiers docstring at line 11
parent_id:  record["parentUuid"]    # repairs the spine
event_ts:   record["timestamp"]     # the result's own timestamp, distinct from the call's
payload:
  tool_use_id:                block["tool_use_id"]
  source_tool_assistant_uuid: record.get("sourceToolAssistantUUID")
  is_error:                   bool(block.get("is_error"))
  tool_denial_kind:           record.get("toolDenialKind")
  raw:                        <scrubbed record>
```

Follow the existing convention: extract flat fields onto the payload, ship the rest via `raw`.
`promptId`, `agentId`, `slug`, `isSidechain` need no extraction — they ride in `raw` like every
other passthrough field, per the decision to keep `raw` as-is and clean up later.

### 2. `src/collector/normalizer/claude_code.py` — new scrub helper

`_scrub_tool_result_for_raw(record) -> dict` — returns a copy with:

- `toolUseResult` removed entirely (every key under it is tool output or file content)
- each `message.content[]` block of type `tool_result` given `content = _CONTENT_PLACEHOLDER`

Mirrors the shape of `_scrub_record_for_raw` (line 134). **Unconditional** — not gated on
`config.redact_generated_file_content`. That flag governs generated *source* in Write/Edit inputs;
tool output is categorically never shipped, so it must not be switchable. Same reasoning as the
`_GENERATED_CONTENT_FIELDS` comment at line 34-36.

`toolUseResult` is still *read* first for derivation in `_merge_tool_result` (line 553) and only
scrubbed on the way into `raw` — that ordering already exists and stays.

### 3. `src/collector/normalizer/claude_code.py` — Task results

**`_handle_spawn`** (line 314): register the spawn in `open_tool_calls` so its `tool_result` merges,
the same way `_handle_assistant` does for ordinary tool calls (line 303). Extract `status`,
`agent_id`, and `resolved_model` from `toolUseResult` onto the `sub_agent_spawn` payload.

Note `toolUseResult.prompt` (the subagent's task text) is user content — it must be scrubbed by the
same helper as everything else under `toolUseResult`, i.e. dropped with the whole object.

### 4. Tests that currently encode the bug

Two existing assertions will fail and are correct to change:

- `tests/collector/normalizer/test_tool_pairing.py:39`
  `test_event_order_matches_file_order_no_event_for_tool_result` — asserts the exact event sequence
  with no `tool_result`. Rename and update to expect the event in file order.
- `tests/collector/normalizer/test_shape_contract.py:161` — the allowed `event_type` set; add
  `"tool_result"`.

## Tests

New file `tests/collector/normalizer/test_tool_result_events.py`, using the existing `normalizer` /
`normalize_one` fixtures (`tests/collector/normalizer/conftest.py`) and
`tests/fixtures/normalizer/sessions.py` builders:

1. **Event is emitted, in file order** — `tool_pairing_session()` yields a `tool_result` event for
   each of `toolu_bash1` / `toolu_edit1`, positioned between the events it follows.
2. **Spine repairs** — every event's `parent_id`, where non-null, resolves to some event's
   `record_id` in the same session. This is the regression guard for the 16% dangling rate; it must
   also hold for `mixed_model_subagent_session()`.
3. **`sourceToolAssistantUUID` survives** onto `payload["source_tool_assistant_uuid"]`.
4. **`is_error` / `toolDenialKind`** — a denied call (new fixture case, `toolDenialKind:
   "user-rejected"`, no `toolUseResult`) emits a `tool_result` event with `is_error` True and
   `tool_denial_kind` set, and does not crash on the missing `toolUseResult`.
5. **Redaction — the load-bearing test.** For every emitted event across every fixture builder,
   assert `"toolUseResult" not in payload["raw"]` and that no `tool_result` block in
   `raw.message.content` has a `content` value other than the placeholder. Assert the known
   fixture strings (`"1 failed, 4 passed"`, `"...file contents..."`) appear nowhere in the
   serialized session. Extend `tests/collector/normalizer/test_redaction.py` with the same check
   driven by `redact_generated_file_content=False` config, proving the scrub is unconditional.
6. **Derivation unchanged** — the existing `tool_call` assertions in `test_tool_pairing.py`
   (`exit_status`, `duration_ms`, `bytes_read`, `hunks`, `lines_added/removed`) still pass, proving
   `toolUseResult` is read before it is scrubbed.
7. **Subagent outcome** — `mixed_model_subagent_session()`: the `sub_agent_spawn` for the child that
   does return a result carries `status` / `resolved_model`; `toolu_spawn_haiku`, whose result never
   arrives, keeps null placeholders (the fixture already covers this case at sessions.py:321).
8. **Idempotency** — `test_losslessness.py::test_run_twice_idempotency` covers the new event type
   automatically; confirm it still passes.

## Verification

1. `pytest tests/collector/normalizer/ -q` — the module's own suite.
2. `pytest tests/collector/ -q` — catches downstream assumptions in `test_engine.py` /
   `test_dump_transport.py` about event types.
3. **Corpus re-run** — re-normalize the 9 sessions in
   `/Users/sumandra/projects/talium/traces/Users/sumandra/.claude/projects/-Users-sumandra-projects-talium-code-econ`
   via `src/collector/cli_normalize.py` and assert against the pre-fix baseline:
   - dangling `parent_id` count: **131 → 0** in `1cc0fed2`, and 0 across all sessions
   - `tool_result` events: **0 → 4,996** corpus-wide
   - `source_tool_assistant_uuid` non-null on 100% of them
   - `tool_denial_kind` non-null on 40
   - grep the output for `"toolUseResult"` and for known stdout strings — **zero hits**
4. `git diff` review of the scrub helper specifically — it is the seam where a redaction bypass
   would be easiest to introduce.

### 6.11 How turns are identified — and a real gotcha in doing it

**There is no `turn_id` field.** Nothing in the output says "these N events are turn #7." A
consumer reconstructs turn boundaries from three signals:

1. **A `user_message` conventionally starts a turn** — everything until the next
   `user_message` belongs to it.
2. **`parent_id` chains the records together** within that span, in order.

git commit -q -F - <<'EOF'
Normalizer: restore tool_result, cap attachment bodies, mark token scope

Four fidelity and redaction fixes to the Claude Code normalizer, each verified
against a 10-session / 62-subagent reference corpus.

tool_result records were dropped entirely: _handle_user merged their derived
fields into the open tool_call and returned without emitting. That broke the
uuid/parentUuid spine (16% of assistant events had an unresolvable parent_id)
and hid every rejected call. They now ship as their own event with
toolUseResult and the block content stripped. Task results additionally fold
status/resolved_model/duration_ms onto sub_agent_spawn, which previously had no
merge target at all.

Session discovery now recognises a transcript by shape -- <project>/<session>.jsonl
at depth 2 -- instead of accepting any .jsonl outside subagents/. A transcript
found at the wrong depth still parses, so it normalised "successfully" while its
subagents were searched for beside the wrong directory and silently resolved to
nothing.

Thinking block signatures are dropped: 3.44MB across the corpus, 11% of raw
transcript bytes, unreadable, and not a usable proxy for anything (r=0.37
against output_tokens). The plaintext is already absent in every observed
version, so has_thinking now carries the remaining signal explicitly.

Attachment records are promoted out of `unknown` and their bodies capped by
config. Several types embed whole files -- the largest observed is 66,739 chars
-- which defeated the Write/Edit scrubbing two records away. Length is policy
(attachment_len, per-type overrides, a separate default-deny for unrecognised
types); which fields hold the body is structural. Artifact classification
(extension/basename/mime) rides alongside, with mime extracted from MCP results
before the scrub since remote artifacts produce no file_change.

assistant_message gains message_id, first_block_of_message and usage_scope.
Claude Code repeats the whole usage block on every record it splits a response
across, so summing token fields over-counted 2.09x with nothing in the output
saying so. Additive: the values are untouched, and the flag reproduces the
independently computed total exactly.

Contract regenerated; the diff is pure insertions with no removals.
EOF

That is no longer true — the chain is unbroken, and dangling parents are zero across the whole reference corpus. Rewrite it. Also fold in what was measured about turn identification, which supersedes the section's guidance:
   - `promptId` is present on every user record — real prompts *and* tool_results — so a promptId run spans a whole turn. 127 runs across the corpus, zero non-contiguous.

   - `file-history-snapshot` with `isSnapshotUpdate == false` opens a turn; count equals turns + 1 (the session baseline). Update-snapshots fire mid-turn and must be filtered.
   - Turn attribution itself is deliberately NOT done in the normalizer — it belongs to graph construction, walking `uuid`/`parentUuid` from a promptId-bearing record bounded by `turn_duration` or the next `promptId`. The thinking *plaintext* is empty in all 2,382 blocks across agent versions 2.1.202–2.1.220 — Claude Code strips it before writing the transcript. New `has_thinking` field. `thinking_char_count` is retained and is NOT dead: null means no thinking block, 0 means one present with no text. input.plan:
# Finishing the normalizer: intent signal, attachment clarity, vendor seam, published schema

## Context

Phases 1–3 fixed fidelity and redaction (`32be5c3`), Phase 4 brought the docs back in line
(`52be2f8`). Five things remain before the normalizer is done and we can move to the causal
graph design.

They are not loose ends of the same kind. (1) and (2) are about *keeping the right signal* now
that we are capping content — get these wrong and the graph is built on data that cannot answer
the intent question. (4) and (5) are about *contracts*: the normalizer is about to have a second
vendor and a downstream consumer, and neither seam exists yet. (3) is bookkeeping that stops the
graph design starting from claims we have already disproved.

**Prior decisions this round rests on:** content length is policy and lives in config; which
fields hold content is structural and lives in code; the normalizer only ever adds to `payload`
and only ever removes from `raw`; anything needed from a region about to be scrubbed is
extracted first.

---

## 1. Assistant text cap — the intent signal

**Why.** Assistant text is the best available signal of *intent* — whether the agent is about to
review, implement, or fix. Claude's thinking plaintext is gone (measured empty in all 2,382
blocks), so this is what remains. The task-classification design that consumes it comes after the
causal graph; the job now is to make sure the signal survives capping.

- `NormalizerConfig.assistant_text_len: int = 1000` — `-1` keeps all, `0` drops, `N` truncates.
  1000 is a deliberate guess, not a measurement: median assistant text is 93 chars and only 12%
  of blocks exceed 1k, so this keeps ~88% of blocks whole while bounding the tail.
- Applied to `text` blocks in `raw.message.content[]` on assistant records, via a
  `_scrub_assistant_text_for_raw` chained where `_scrub_thinking_for_raw` already is.
- `text_char_count` is computed from the **unscrubbed** `message`, which `_make_assistant_message`
  already receives separately from `raw_record` — verify that ordering holds and add
  `text_truncated: bool` alongside, mirroring `attachment.content_truncated`.

**Explicitly not doing:** capping `user_message` text. The prompt *is* the primary intent signal
and prompts are short. Recorded as a decision, not an oversight — revisit if corpus data says
otherwise.

**Note for Codex:** `event_msg/agent_reasoning.text` and `response_item/reasoning.content` are
populated in real Codex sessions — the opposite of Claude. Whatever cap policy lands here must
cover them when the Codex normalizer is written.

## 2. Attachment type clarity

**Why.** "It's a `file`" is lossy. Some attachments are startup context that effectively becomes
the system prompt; others are a mid-session @-mention. Measured: **CLAUDE.md arrives via
`hook_success` / `hook_additional_context` on the `SessionStart` hook (8 each), never as a `file`
attachment.** The startup cluster is also positionally distinct (median record index 3–16 vs
191–479 for mid-session types), and several types self-declare with `isInitial`.

Promote per-type identity onto the payload so none of this requires digging into `raw`. The body
stays capped; identity and size never are.

| Types | Promote |
|---|---|
| `file`, `already_read_file`, `edited_text_file`, `opened_file_in_ide`, `selected_lines_in_ide`, `compact_file_reference`, `directory` | `path`, `display_path`, `extension`, `artifact_class`, `total_lines` |
| `skill_listing` | `skill_names[]`, `skill_count`, `is_initial` |
| `agent_listing_delta` | `added_types[]`, `is_initial` |
| `deferred_tools_delta` | `added_names[]`, `removed_names[]` |
| `hook_success`, `hook_additional_context` | `hook_name`, `hook_event`, `exit_code`, `duration_ms` |

Plus one derived field on every attachment:

- **`is_startup_context: bool`** — true when `hookEvent == "SessionStart"` or `isInitial` is
  true. This is the field that answers "was this part of the system prompt", which is otherwise
  only inferable from record position.

Field paths go in the existing `_ATTACHMENT_CONTENT_FIELDS` neighbourhood in `claude_code.py`
(structural); nothing here is config.

## 3. Findings ledger, and retract the addendum

**Why.** `notes/` is thought and experiment; it gets distilled into design. The causal-graph
design has not been written, and the addendum would actively mislead it.

- **New `docs/design/notes/findings-ledger.md`** — dated, one entry per measured finding, each
  with its evidence and what it implies. Seed it with what this conversation established:
  thinking plaintext empty across 6 versions; signature 3.44MB/11% of bytes with r=0.37;
  `turn_duration` not universal and the 113/11/3 classification; `promptId` runs as the turn key
  (127 runs, 0 non-contiguous); token scoping 2.09× (3.89× via `raw`); OTEL parity on tool
  inputs, span tree, permission-wait; OTEL carries PII, JSONL does not; Codex structure and its
  three divergences.
- **`claude-code-session-observability-addendum.md` gets a RETRACTED banner** naming the three
  claims measurement disproved: thinking text is JSONL-only (it is absent), tool inputs are
  JSONL-only (OTEL has `full_command`/`tool_input`), OTEL has no tree (553/569 spans parented).
  The file stays as history; the banner stops §2A being built on.

## 4. Vendor seam — scaffold only

**Why.** Everything is written for Claude JSONL. The seam has to exist before Codex, but Codex
itself waits: its real divergences (no `uuid`/`parentUuid` chain, reasoning text present,
explicit `turn_context` boundaries) are causal-graph model questions, not normalizer questions.

# Normalizer Completion

Full plan: `docs/plan/2026-08-07-normalizer-completion.md` (in-repo, readable).

## Context

Phases 1–3 fixed fidelity and redaction (`32be5c3`); Phase 4 brought the docs in line
(`52be2f8`). Five changes close out the normalizer before causal-graph design starts. Two are
about keeping the intent signal now that content is capped; two are contracts that do not exist
yet (a second vendor, a downstream consumer); one is bookkeeping so the graph design does not
start from disproved claims.

## Steps

1. **Text caps.** `assistant_text_len = 1000`, `user_meta_text_len = 1000` applied only to
   `isMeta` records. Typed prompts (`origin.kind == "human"`) ship whole. Driven by a measured
   151,597-char skill body arriving as an `isMeta` user message.
2. **Attachment identity.** Promote `path`/`skill_names`/`hook_name`/etc. onto the payload, add
   `is_startup_context` (`hookEvent == SessionStart` or `isInitial`). CLAUDE.md arrives via the
   SessionStart hook, never as a `file` attachment.
3. **Vendor seam, scaffold only.** `-t claude|codex` in `utils/test_normalizer.sh`, `--vendor` on
   `cli_normalize`, dispatch through the existing `normalizer.registry`, Codex stub. No Codex
   parser — its three divergences (no parent chain, reasoning text present, explicit turns) are
   causal-graph questions.
4. **`meta_info` wrap.** `cli_normalize` output becomes `{meta_info, sessions}`. Breaking for
   readers of the bare array.
5. **Published artifacts.** `src/common/events/{payload.json, normalized_schema.json}`, generated
   by `cli_publish_payload.py`, deriving from the promoted `_derive_shape`.
   `test_shape_contract.py` stays the drift guard.
6. **Findings ledger** + RETRACTED banner on the observability addendum.

Order: 1–3 independent; 4 before 5; 6 anytime.

## Verification

- `pytest tests/ -q` green; shape-contract diff is pure insertions.
- Corpus re-run over 10 real sessions: dangling `parent_id` 0, `tool_result` 2,197, denials
  20/7/2/2, zero leaks from both probes.
- Per-step assertions listed in §11 of the in-repo plan.

def test_cli_rejects_an_unknown_vendor(tmp_path, capsys):
    from collector import cli_normalize

    session = recorded_sessions.RECORDED_DIR / "session-regular.jsonl"
    with pytest.raises(SystemExit) as excinfo:
        cli_normalize.main([str(session), "--out", str(tmp_path / "o.json"), "--vendor", "cursor"])

input.command:
git commit -q -F - <<'EOF'
Normalizer: text caps, attachment identity, vendor seam, published contract

Closes out the normalizer before causal-graph design. Each change verified
against a 10-session / 62-subagent corpus spanning agent versions 2.1.202
through 2.1.220.

Text is the surviving intent signal -- Claude Code strips thinking plaintext
before persisting, empty in all 1,413 blocks observed -- so assistant text is
what a task classifier will have to work from. Capped at 1k, which leaves 88%
of blocks whole. Injected user records are capped too; typed prompts are not.
Identifying an injection needs four markers, not one: isMeta misses the
post-compaction summary (30,726 chars) and the task-notification (20,320). It
fails open, because the unmarked population turned out to be subagent task
prompts -- the directive handed to a child agent, which is intent, not noise.

Attachments now carry their identity on the payload rather than only in raw,
so "which skill was in context" survives a zeroed body. is_startup_context
separates context that effectively becomes the system prompt from a mid-session
mention; CLAUDE.md, measured, arrives via the SessionStart hook and never as a
file attachment. sub_agent_spawn gains the Task description and prompt size for
the same reason -- labelling a subagent's work should not require reading raw.

Fixes a scrub bypass found while wiring that: _handle_spawn took the unscrubbed
record, so a spawn sharing its assistant record with a long text block or an
Edit shipped content every sibling event had scrubbed.

cli_normalize dispatches through the existing normalizer.registry and a
parallel SOURCE_READERS map instead of naming ClaudeCodeNormalizer directly.
Codex is a stub that raises rather than returning an empty SessionSource: an
empty result is indistinguishable from a session that had no records, and would
batch-normalize 19 real files to silent nothing. Its shape is understood; what
record_id/parent_id mean for a vendor with no parent chain is a causal-graph
decision.

Output gains a meta_info envelope carrying schema_version, collector_version,
a digest of the resolved config, and counts -- provenance the sessions have
nowhere to hold. Breaking for readers of the bare array.

The event contract is now published at src/common/events/, derived from real
output rather than hand-written, with payload.json as the readable example and
normalized_schema.json as the exhaustive contract. Derivation is shared between
the generator and the drift guard so the two cannot measure different things.
Supersedes tests/sample-data/normalizer-shape-contract.json.

Adds a findings ledger recording what measurement showed, and retracts the
observability addendum: its three arguments for a JSONL spine -- thinking is
JSONL-only, tool inputs are JSONL-only, OTEL has no tree -- are all false.
EOF

# -- ai-title: session-level, plucked once (§6.2) -------------------------------------------


def _with_ai_title(*titles, at=2):
    """CC never emits ai-title at record 0 -- earliest observed is index 8 -- so the fixture
    inserts it after the session has started, which is what forces the backfill."""
    src = sessions.simple_session()
    for offset, title in enumerate(titles):
        src.records.insert(at + offset, {"type": "ai-title", "aiTitle": title, "sessionId": "session-simple"})
    return src


def test_ai_title_lifted_onto_session_start(normalizer, normalize_one):
    session = normalize_one(normalizer, _with_ai_title("Brainstorm event messaging architecture"))
    start = next(e for e in session.events if e.event_type == "session_start")
    assert start.payload["ai_title"] == "Brainstorm event messaging architecture"


def test_repeats_do_not_multiply_the_field(normalizer, normalize_one):
    """3-42 identical records per session in the corpus. The point is one field, not N."""
    session = normalize_one(normalizer, _with_ai_title(*(["Add Mermaid diagrams"] * 12)))
    starts = [e for e in session.events if e.event_type == "session_start"]
    assert len(starts) == 1
    assert starts[0].payload["ai_title"] == "Add Mermaid diagrams"


def test_first_title_wins(normalizer, normalize_one):
    """No observed session changes its title. If one ever does, the first is the label that
    described the work as it was happening."""
    session = normalize_one(normalizer, _with_ai_title("First goal", "Revised goal"))
    start = next(e for e in session.events if e.event_type == "session_start")
    assert start.payload["ai_title"] == "First goal"


def test_absent_title_is_null_not_missing(normalizer, normalize_one):
    session = normalize_one(normalizer, sessions.simple_session())
    start = next(e for e in session.events if e.event_type == "session_start")
    assert start.payload["ai_title"] is None


def test_records_still_ship_as_passthrough(normalizer, normalize_one):
    """§9 has no silent ignore-list: lifting the value does not delete the records."""
    session = normalize_one(normalizer, _with_ai_title(*(["Same title"] * 3)))
    passthrough = [e for e in session.events
                   if e.event_type == "unknown" and e.payload["raw"].get("type") == "ai-title"]
    assert len(passthrough) == 3


def test_subagent_sessions_have_no_title(normalizer):
    """No subagent stream in the corpus carries one; the parent's must not leak down."""
    for session in normalizer.normalize(sessions.mixed_model_subagent_session()):
        start = next(e for e in session.events if e.event_type == "session_start")
        assert start.payload["ai_title"] is None

cat > docs/design/notes/claude_token_usage.md <<'EOF'
# Token Counts in Claude Code Transcripts

What the session files record about tokens, and what they leave out.

Measured over the reference corpus: 9,188 assistant records, 4,472 separate model
responses, taken from `~/.claude/projects/-Users-sumandra-projects-talium-code-econ`
(main sessions, subagents, and the stray `memory/` transcript).

## 1. In short

- The transcript has **no count of thinking tokens**. No such field exists anywhere.
- Thinking is still **paid for**. It is counted inside `output_tokens`, mixed in with
  the visible reply.
- So you can see what thinking cost in total, but you cannot pull it out on its own.
- The length of the thinking block's `signature` string rises and falls with the amount
  of thinking. It is the only handle left on how much a response thought.

## 2. Every token field the transcript carries

All key paths found under `message.usage`, across all 9,188 assistant records:

```
input_tokens                                  tokens sent
output_tokens                                 tokens produced (see §3)
cache_read_input_tokens                       read back from cache
cache_creation_input_tokens                   written to cache
cache_creation.ephemeral_5m_input_tokens      cache written, 5 minute life
cache_creation.ephemeral_1h_input_tokens      cache written, 1 hour life
service_tier                                  which service level served it
inference_geo                                 where it ran
speed                                         speed setting
server_tool_use.web_search_requests           web searches made
server_tool_use.web_fetch_requests            page fetches made
iterations[]                                  repeat of the six count fields above
```

Nothing named for thinking or reasoning. No breakdown of `output_tokens` into parts.

`iterations[]` is a copy, not a split by phase. Its first entry matched the top-level
numbers in every record checked (0 mismatches out of 5,480).

## 3. Thinking is counted inside output_tokens

Compare responses whose only visible content is a tool call. There is no reply text to
muddy the count, so any difference in tokens is the thinking.

| response contains        |     n | median `output_tokens` |
| ------------------------ | ----: | ---------------------: |
| tool call                | 1,228 |                    232 |
| tool call **+ thinking** | 1,418 |                    381 |

Same pattern when reply text is present:

| response contains               |    n | median `output_tokens` |
| ------------------------------- | ---: | ---------------------: |
| text + tool call                |  437 |                    313 |
| text + tool call **+ thinking** |  743 |                    628 |
| text                            |  120 |                    410 |
| text **+ thinking**             |  180 |                  1,318 |

Another way to see it: for replies that are text only, count characters per output
token. Without thinking it is 2.59. With thinking it drops to 1.44 — far more tokens
than the visible words account for. The extra tokens are the thinking.

## 4. Signature length tracks how much was thought

A thinking block keeps a `signature` string. It cannot be read or decoded. But its
length moves with the amount of thinking.

Tool-call-only responses again, so no reply text is involved (n = 1,418):

| `signature` length | n     | median `output_tokens` |
| ------------------ | ----- | ---------------------: |
| under 400          | 82    |                    171 |
| 400 – 800          | 611   |                    222 |
| 800 – 1,600        | 305   |                    427 |
| 1,600 and over     | 420   |                  1,445 |

The two move together closely (correlation 0.87). Fitting a line through them gives a
starting point of 289 tokens before any thinking — close to the 232 measured for the
same kind of response with no thinking block at all.

A response can show zero visible characters and still bill 1,445 output tokens.

## 5. The thinking text itself is gone

Total thinking plaintext across the whole corpus: **0 characters**. Every thinking block
has the field but it is always empty. Claude Code strips the words before writing the
file. Only the `signature` survives, and it holds 6,547,484 characters across 2,382
blocks — 3.7 times the size of all attachment content combined.

## 6. Reading rule: use the finished record

One model response is split across several lines in the file, all sharing one
`message.id`. The unfinished lines carry a partial count.

- Unfinished line: `stop_reason` is `null`, `output_tokens` is a small number like 2 or 3.
- Finished line: `stop_reason` is set (`tool_use`, `end_turn`, `stop_sequence`), and
  `output_tokens` is the real total.

Half the lines are unfinished ones: 2,266 of 4,472 first-seen records had
`output_tokens` under 10, and 2,258 of those had no `stop_reason`.

**Group by `message.id`, then take the count from the line that has a `stop_reason`.**
Any other choice gives numbers that are wrong and that look backwards — thinking will
appear to *lower* the token count.

Finished-line totals: lowest 0, middle 357, highest 34,946. 4,126 of the 4,472 responses
have a finished line; the remaining 346 were cut off and have no final count.

## 7. What this means for us

- Total cost per response is trustworthy, once §6 is followed.
- Cost cannot be split into thinking versus answering. Not from this file.
- Dropping the `signature` blob is right — it is 3.44 MB and unreadable — but its
  **length** is worth keeping as a number before it goes. It is roughly 30 bytes and it
  is the only measure of thinking effort available.
- If a future Claude Code version adds a thinking count, it belongs here and this note
  should be revisited.
EOF

input.plan:
# Thinking-Token Recovery via Tokenizer

## Context

Claude Code transcripts carry no thinking-token count. Thinking is billed inside
`output_tokens`, mixed with the visible reply — measured and documented in
`docs/design/notes/claude_token_usage.md` (39% of all output tokens in the corpus).

Cost attribution for the causal graph (question 2, budget hotspots) needs the split. It is
recoverable by subtraction:

```
thinking_tokens = output_tokens - tokens(visible content)
```

The visible content — reply text and the tool arguments the model generated — is present in
the JSONL before we redact it. Counting it needs a tokenizer.

**Why a tokenizer, not a fitted ratio.** A character-per-token ratio regressed from this
corpus would encode one person's content mix into the estimator. The corpus is 146 files
across 5 projects, 129 of them one project. It is fit to validate an independent estimator's
error; it is not a sound basis for deriving one. tiktoken is approximate against Claude's
vocabulary but is a real BPE tokenizer, and its error is a property of the tokenizer rather
than of our sample.

## Step 1 — Bake-off (throwaway, not committed)

Script in scratchpad. Decides the encoding before any source change.

**Ground truth.** Responses containing no thinking block: there `output_tokens` *is* the
visible token count, exactly. ~1,779 such responses. Used to measure error only — no
parameter is fitted from it.

**Candidates.**

```
o200k_base     tiktoken, GPT-4o/o-series vocab, 200k    primary candidate
cl100k_base    tiktoken, GPT-4/3.5 vocab, 100k          older, denser on code
chars / 4      naive reference, no dependency           baseline to beat
```

**What gets tokenized**, per assistant record, matching what the model actually emitted:

```
text block      -> block["text"]
tool_use block  -> block["name"] + json.dumps(block["input"])
```

Summed across records sharing one `message.id`, compared against that response's
`output_tokens` taken from the record carrying a `stop_reason` (see §6 of the token-usage
note — unfinished records carry partial counts and will silently corrupt this).

**Report.** Signed error distribution, median/p90/p99, stratified by model and by response
shape. The decisive question is the *shape* of the error:

- **Constant per-block offset** → structural framing the tokenizer cannot see (block type,
  id, JSON envelope). Correctable with a structural constant, and legitimate.
- **Proportional drift** → vocabulary mismatch. Not correctable. Report it and live with it.

Do not fit a scale factor to close a proportional gap — that is the mistake this step exists
to avoid.

**Exit criterion.** Pick the encoding with the lowest p90 absolute error. If no candidate
beats roughly 15% p90, stop and reconsider rather than shipping a number nobody can trust.

## Step 2 — Normalizer: count before redaction

New `src/collector/normalizer/tokens.py`:

```python
count_visible_output_tokens(record, encoding) -> (tokens: int, text_chars: int, arg_chars: int)
```

Encoding object loaded once and cached at module level; tiktoken's is expensive to build.

**Call site.** `claude_code.py::_handle_assistant`, on the untouched `record`, **before**
line 621 where `raw_record` is built. This ordering is load-bearing: `_scrub_record_for_raw`
strips Write/Edit content, and that content is generated output tokens. Counting after the
scrub undercounts exactly the largest responses. The existing seam already keeps `record` and
`raw_record` separate, so no restructuring is needed.

**Emitted on `assistant_message`:**

```
visible_output_tokens   int   tokenizer count for this record's blocks
tokenizer               str   encoding name, e.g. "o200k_base"
text_chars              int   fallback + drift signal
tool_arg_chars          int   fallback + drift signal
```

Per record, block-scoped — content is split across records the same way. Chars ride along
because they are free and let a future tokenizer change be sanity-checked against stored
data.

`tokenizer` is stored per event on purpose: a count is only interpretable against the vocab
that produced it, and the encoding will eventually change.

**Config** (`config.py`): `tokenizer_encoding: str = "o200k_base"`,
`count_visible_output_tokens: bool = True`.

**Dependency:** `tiktoken` in `requirements.txt`. MIT, maintained by OpenAI, widely used.
Rejected: `claude-tokenizer` / `anthropic-tokenizer-typescript` (Claude 1/2 only,
deprecated — wrong vocab for Claude 3+); community HuggingFace "Claude" vocabs
(reverse-engineered, unverified); `transformers` (heavy, and has no Claude vocab either).

**Operational note:** tiktoken fetches its BPE vocab on first use. Set `TIKTOKEN_CACHE_DIR`
and confirm offline behaviour before this runs anywhere without network.

## Step 3 — Derive thinking in the analysis layer

Not in the normalizer. Same split already agreed for turn segmentation: the normalizer emits
per-record facts, cross-record derivation belongs to graph construction.

```
group events by message_id
visible = sum(visible_output_tokens)
thinking = output_tokens - visible        # output_tokens from the first_block event
```

Negative results are expected where true thinking is near zero (8.7% of responses under the
character model). Floor at zero and set a flag — never clamp silently, since a rising
negative rate is the signal that the tokenizer has drifted from Claude's.

## Step 4 — Republish and document

- Regenerate `src/common/events/{normalized_schema.json, payload.json}` via
  `cli_publish_payload.py`; `test_shape_contract.py` diff must be pure insertions.
- `docs/modules/normalizer.md`: the new fields and the count-before-redaction ordering.
- `docs/design/notes/claude_token_usage.md`: new section with the bake-off result and the
  honest error bars.

## Also pending (fold in or defer — your call)

- `thinking_signature_chars` — the TODO now in `claude_code.py::_scrub_thinking_for_raw`.
  Independent cross-check on thinking volume, and cheap alongside this.
- `meta_info` is still not covered by the published schema.

Both touch the same schema republish, so doing them together avoids a second pass.

## Verification

- `pytest tests/ -q` green (currently 1215 passed, 26 skipped).
- Bake-off error table reproduced from committed corpus; numbers land in the note.
- Corpus re-run: `visible_output_tokens` present on every `assistant_message`; zero events
  where it exceeds the response's `output_tokens` by more than the measured p99.
- Redaction ordering proven by test: a Write call with a large body must count the body and
  still redact it from `raw`.
- Existing leak probes stay clean.

import json,glob,os,statistics,collections
import tiktoken
e=tiktoken.get_encoding('o200k_base')
R=1.52   # vocabulary conversion, measured on prose (tight, ±6%, same in both encodings)
agg={}
for p in glob.glob(os.path.expanduser('~/.claude/projects')+'/**/*.jsonl',recursive=True):
    proj=p.split('/projects/')[1].split('/')[0]
    for l in open(p,errors='replace'):
        if not l.strip(): continue
        try: r=json.loads(l)
        except: continue
        if r.get('type')!='assistant': continue
        m=r.get('message') or {}; mid=m.get('id')
        if not mid: continue
        d=agg.setdefault(mid,{'out':None,'kinds':set(),'text':[],'tools':[],'model':m.get('model'),'proj':proj})
        if m.get('stop_reason') is not None:
            u=m.get('usage') or {}
            if u.get('output_tokens') is not None: d['out']=u['output_tokens']
        for b in m.get('content') or []:
            if not isinstance(b,dict): continue
            d['kinds'].add(b.get('type'))
            if b.get('type')=='text': d['text'].append(b.get('text') or '')
            elif b.get('type')=='tool_use': d['tools'].append((b.get('name') or '',b.get('input') or {}))

def tok(d):
    q=list(d['text'])
    for n,a in d['tools']: q+=[n,json.dumps(a,separators=(', ',': '),ensure_ascii=False)]
    return len(e.encode(''.join(q),disallowed_special=()))

truth=[d for d in agg.values() if d['out'] and d['out']>0 and 'thinking' not in d['kinds']]
wt=[d for d in truth if d['tools']]
# solve per-response for the framing constant
K=[(d['out']-R*tok(d))/len(d['tools']) for d in wt]
K.sort()
p=lambda q,v=K: v[int(q*len(v))]
print(f'per-tool-call framing overhead K, solved per response (n={len(K)}):')
print(f'  p10={p(.10):.0f}  p25={p(.25):.0f}  median={p(.50):.0f}  p75={p(.75):.0f}  p90={p(.90):.0f}')

print('\nis K structural? (stable across model / project / call count)')
for lbl,key in (('model',lambda d:d['model']),('project',lambda d:d['proj'][:44]),
                ('n tool calls',lambda d:min(len(d['tools']),3))):
    print(f'  by {lbl}:')
    g=collections.defaultdict(list)
    for d in wt: g[key(d)].append((d['out']-R*tok(d))/len(d['tools']))
    for k,v in sorted(g.items(),key=lambda x:-len(x[1])):
        if len(v)>=40: print(f'    {str(k):46} n={len(v):<5} median K={statistics.median(v):>6.0f}')

K0=statistics.median(K)
print(f'\n=== MODEL: output_tokens = {R} * tiktoken(content) + {K0:.0f} * n_tool_calls ===')
for lbl,rows in (('text only',[d for d in truth if not d['tools']]),
                 ('with tool calls',wt),('ALL',truth)):

## 6. Reading rule: use the finished record

One model response is split across several lines in the file, all sharing one
`message.id`. The unfinished lines carry a partial count.

- Unfinished line: `stop_reason` is `null`, `output_tokens` is a small number like 2 or 3.
- Finished line: `stop_reason` is set (`tool_use`, `end_turn`, `stop_sequence`), and
  `output_tokens` is the real total.

Half the lines are unfinished ones: 2,266 of 4,472 first-seen records had
`output_tokens` under 10, and 2,258 of those had no `stop_reason`.

**Group by `message.id`, then take the count from the line that has a `stop_reason`.**
Any other choice gives numbers that are wrong and that look backwards — thinking will
appear to *lower* the token count.

measurement, not missing content. Corrected for it, `output_tokens` **is** the token count
of the visible reply, exactly. Nothing is hidden inside it. Subtraction works.

## 8. How many tokens a piece of text is worth

Anthropic does not publish a tokenizer we can run on our own machine. `tiktoken` is
OpenAI's, runs locally, and is close but not the same. How close depends on the model:

| model | tokens vs `tiktoken` | how we know |
| ----------------- | -------------------: | ---------------------------------- |
| Sonnet 4.6        |               1.13 x | asked Anthropic directly           |
| Claude 5 family   |               1.52 x | from our own files, prose, +/- 6%  |

The tokenizer changed between the two.

on which model wrote the reply and will change again. Stored counts stay correct; the
multiplier lives in config where one edit fixes every session ever recorded.

### How to ask Anthropic for a count

The count service prices a whole request, not a piece of text. To measure one string, ask
twice and subtract — the request wrapper is the same both times, so it cancels:

```
wrapper       = count("a") - 1
text tokens   = count(THE TEXT) - wrapper
```

Two traps, both cost real time:

- The Anthropic Python library **refuses** to count tokens on Bedrock. It raises

  operation underneath works fine. Call `bedrock-runtime count-tokens` through `boto3`.

  `anthropic.claude-sonnet-4-6`. Running takes `us.anthropic.claude-sonnet-4-6`. The
  request body must include `max_tokens` or it is rejected.

- Total cost per response is trustworthy, once section 6 is followed.

input.plan:
# Item 1 — Causal graph consistent with normalized schema 2.0.0

One of four; items 2–4 (thinking estimate, design doc, attrs schema) follow separately.

## Context

The events contract moved to 2.0.0: `visible_output_tokens` was renamed
`estimated_visible_tokens`, and `normalized_schema.json` restructured from
`payload_by_type[type][field] -> [types]` to
`payload_by_type[type] = {description, fields: {field: {types, description}}}`.

**Nothing in `causal_graph` broke.** It does not parse `normalized_schema.json` — the file
appears only in docstrings (`builder.py:6`, `family.py:5`). The graph's own
`models.py:SCHEMA_VERSION = "1.0.0"` is the *graph envelope* version, unrelated to the events
contract, and does not move.

That is luck, not design. `builder.py` reads 25 payload keys through `p.get(...)`, so an
upstream rename yields `None` silently: no exception, no failed test, just nodes with null
attributes and budgets quietly short. Had the builder read `visible_output_tokens`, this
release would have done exactly that. The fix is to make that dependency explicit and checked.

## Changes

**1. Declare the contract dependency.** New `_REQUIRED_PAYLOAD_FIELDS` in
`src/analysis/causal_graph/builder.py`: `event_type -> frozenset(field names)`, covering the
keys the builder reads today:

```
session_start     ai_title
user_message      text, is_injected
assistant_message message_id, first_block_of_message, has_thinking, model,
                  input_tokens, output_tokens, cache_read_tokens, cache_write_tokens
tool_call         tool_name, input, exit_status, duration_ms, files
tool_result       tool_use_id, is_error, tool_denial_kind
sub_agent_spawn   agent_type, child_session_id, resolved_model, status
file_change       derived_from_event_id
```

**2. Guard it.** New `tests/analysis/causal_graph/test_normalized_contract.py`: load
`src/common/events/normalized_schema.json` and assert every declared field is present under
its event type's `fields`. Fails loudly on an upstream rename, naming the field and event type.

Reads the published artifact, not `derive_shape` — the artifact is what a consumer integrates
against, and it is the thing that can go stale.

**Known limit, to state in the test docstring:** this catches *upstream removing a field we
need*. It does not catch *the builder starting to read a field it never declared* — that would
need extraction from source, which is more fragile than the problem it solves.

**3. Docstrings.** `builder.py:6` "schema 1.0.0" → 2.0.0 plus a line on the new nesting, so
the next reader opening `normalized_schema.json` is not surprised by the shape.

## Explicitly not in this item

- Consuming `estimated_visible_tokens` / `tool_call_count` — that is item 2.
- `causal_graph_schema.json` attrs and descriptions — item 4.

### Decisions already taken, for item 2

- **Unmeasured model → ratio 1.0**, not null. Config carries measured ratios (Claude 5 1.52,
  Sonnet 4.6 1.13) and defaults the rest to 1.0, i.e. the raw tiktoken count used unconverted.
  Consequence worth knowing: 1.0 undercounts the visible side for any real Claude model, so
  the derived thinking becomes an **upper bound** rather than a wrong point estimate. Still
  record which ratio was applied and whether it was measured or the default, so a query can
  tell the two apart.
- **Reported beats estimated.** When the source reports a thinking count — Codex publishes one
  today, Claude may later — use it and mark it reported. Estimation is the fallback path, never
  an override.
- **attrs schema derived from built graphs** over the fixture corpus, plus authored
  descriptions and a publish gate, matching `normalized_schema.json`.

## Verification

- `pytest tests/analysis/causal_graph -q` and full `pytest tests/ -q` green (1229 + new).
- Negative check: temporarily rename a field in the declaration to something absent and
  confirm the guard fails naming it, then revert.
- Rebuild a real graph end to end and confirm no attribute silently went null:
  `venv/bin/python -m analysis.causal_graph.cli_graph create <normalized.json>` over a
  session from `traces/nrm_sess`, then confirm assistant nodes still carry non-null
  `output_tokens` and `model`.

ingredients (`estimated_visible_tokens`, `tool_call_count`, per record); the graph is where they
become a number. Constants and their provenance: `docs/design/notes/claude_token_usage.md`.

**Nothing changes in the normalizer.**

## The assistant node today

```json
{ "id": "msg_011CcsUK2HBrhSt7vAeuvk1N", "type": "assistant",
  "ts": "2026-07-10T01:01:00.189Z",
  "attrs": {
    "message_id": "msg_011CcsUK2HBrhSt7vAeuvk1N", "model": "claude-fable-5",
    "has_thinking": true,
    "input_tokens": 65, "output_tokens": 6345,
    "cache_read_tokens": 55341, "cache_write_tokens": 586 },
  "meta": {}, "children": [], "refs": {} }
```

and after:

```json
  "attrs": {
    "message_id": "...", "model": "claude-fable-5", "has_thinking": true,
    "input_tokens": 65, "output_tokens": 6345,
    "cache_read_tokens": 55341, "cache_write_tokens": 586,
    "estimated_reasoning_tokens": 4870,      // NEW
    "reasoning_source": "estimated",         // NEW  reported | estimated
    "reasoning_ratio": 1.52 }                // NEW  ratio actually applied
```

The turn node carries **no** token totals today — `budget` derives them. Reasoning follows the
same path, so the turn reports `input_tokens`, `output_tokens`, `estimated_reasoning_tokens`
through the mechanism that already produces the first two.

## Changes

**1. Contract guard** (was item 1). `_REQUIRED_PAYLOAD_FIELDS` in `builder.py`:
`event_type -> frozenset(fields)` for the 25 payload keys it reads, plus
`tests/analysis/causal_graph/test_normalized_contract.py` asserting each is present in
`src/common/events/normalized_schema.json`.

The builder reads every key through `p.get(...)`, so an upstream rename yields `None` silently
— no exception, no failing test, just null attrs and short budgets. Had it read
`visible_output_tokens`, the 2.0.0 rename would have done exactly that. Catches upstream
*removing* a field we need; does not catch the builder reading one it never declared.
Docstring at `builder.py:6` moves 1.0.0 → 2.0.0 with a note on the new nesting.

**2. Config** — new `src/analysis/causal_graph/config.py`, pydantic + YAML, mirroring
`collector/normalizer/config.py`:

```
tokenizer_ratio_by_model: dict[str, float]   longest-prefix match on model name
                                             claude-opus-5 / sonnet-5 / opus-4-8 / fable-5 -> 1.52
                                             claude-sonnet-4-6 -> 1.13
tokenizer_ratio_default: float = 1.0         unmeasured model: use tiktoken raw, unconverted
tool_call_tokens: int = 27                   fixed block per tool call
tool_call_offset: int = -1                   the constant in 27*n - 1
text_with_tools_tokens: int = 13             text block alongside tool calls
```

Every constant is config, none in code. 1.0 for unmeasured models undercounts the visible side
for any real Claude model, so the estimate becomes an **upper bound** rather than a wrong point
estimate — and `reasoning_ratio: 1.0` on the node says so without a separate flag.

**3. Estimation** — new `src/analysis/causal_graph/reasoning.py`, called from
`_collapse_assistants` in `builder.py:128`, which already has the whole `message_id` group:

```
if payload.reasoning_tokens is not None:        # Codex publishes it; Claude may later
    value, source = payload.reasoning_tokens, "reported"
else:
    visible = ratio * Σ estimated_visible_tokens over the group
    framing = tool_call_tokens * Σ tool_call_count + tool_call_offset   (if any calls)
              + text_with_tools_tokens                                  (if text and calls)
    value, source = output_tokens - visible - framing, "estimated"
```

**Reported always beats estimated** — the branch is on the field's presence, so Codex needs no
special case and a future Claude release needs no code change.

Negatives are floored at 0 (measured ~6.6% of responses, where true reasoning is near zero and
estimator error crosses it). Floor, never silently: a rising negative rate is the signal the
ratio has drifted, so count them and log the rate once per build.

**4. Rollup** — add `estimated_reasoning_tokens` to `TOKEN_FIELDS` in `budget.py:33`.
`_add_assistant` folds every field in that tuple, so turn / assistant / subagent / model
rollups all pick it up with no further change. That *is* the existing principle for token
totals. Also extend `ops.py:turn_tokens` so the derived `tokens` key stays coherent.

**5. Design doc** (was item 3) — `docs/design/causal-graph-design.md`: assistant `attrs` in
§4.1, a subsection on the estimate, and the point that it is **fallback only**. Codex publishes
reasoning counts today and Claude may later; when a count is reported there is no estimation.

## Not in this item

`causal_graph_schema.json` attrs shapes and descriptions — item 4, derived from built graphs
over the fixture corpus plus authored descriptions and a publish gate, matching
`normalized_schema.json`.

## Open, needs a call

`has_thinking` keeps the vendor's word while the new fields use "reasoning". It comes straight
from the normalizer and renaming it graph-side would break the mirror. Left as-is; say if you
want it `has_reasoning` in the graph.

End to end, from a raw session file to an answer. Every output below is real, from
`1791a8da-…` (539 records, 202 nodes, 16 turns).

### 1. Get a normalized envelope

The graph does not read Claude Code transcripts; it reads the normalizer's output.

```bash
venv/bin/python -m collector.cli_normalize \\
    ~/.claude/projects/<project>/<session>.jsonl --out session.normalized.json
```

That writes `{meta_info, sessions: [...]}` — one entry per session, subagents included.

### 2. Build the family

```python
import json
from analysis.causal_graph import build_family

envelope = json.load(open("session.normalized.json"))
family = build_family(envelope)
```

One call. It builds a `Graph` per session and links subagents to their parent.

### 3. Work with it

`build_family` returns a `Family` — the master graph plus its subagent graphs:

```python
family.master.session_id      # '1791a8da-9b5f-45c1-917b-d97d8cec9e28'
family.master.vendor          # 'claude_code'
len(family.master.nodes)      # 202     nodes, keyed by id
len(family.master.roots)      # 16      turn ids, in order
len(family.children)          # 0       subagent graphs, keyed by session_id

family.all_graphs()           # [master, *children]
family.resolve(session_id)    # Graph | None  -- None if that child isn't loaded
```

Nodes are a flat dict keyed by id; structure lives in `children` (ids) and `refs`:

```python
turn = family.master.nodes[family.master.roots[0]]
turn.attrs
# {'prompt_id': '70400655-…', 'status': 'empty', 'duration_ms': 26256}

[family.master.nodes[c].type for c in turn.children]
# ['user_prompt', 'assistant', 'assistant', 'assistant']
```

Every node is `{id, type, ts, attrs, meta, children, refs}`. `attrs` is builder-extracted
and fixed per type; `meta` is the open bag later features write to. A tool node:

```python
{ "id": "toolu_01N2fvBhnqB87yRYUFfLfje4", "type": "tool",
  "ts": "2026-07-10T00:41:07.247Z",
  "attrs": { "tool_name": "Bash", "input": {...},
             "exit_status": 1, "is_error": true,
             "duration_ms": null, "blocked_on_user_ms": null,
             "tool_denial_kind": null },
  "meta": {}, "children": [], "refs": {} }
```

An assistant node — one per API response, tokens from the `fb=true` record:

```python
{ "id": "msg_011CcsXMKFK4NeAaYx9TsYYt", "type": "assistant",
  "attrs": { "model": "claude-fable-5", "has_thinking": true,
             "input_tokens": 2, "output_tokens": 1247,

             "estimated_reasoning_tokens": 291,     # billed INSIDE output_tokens

```

`estimated_reasoning_tokens` is **inside** `output_tokens`, not on top of it — reasoning is
billed there and never broken out. It is an estimate unless `reasoning_source` says
`reported`. See `docs/design/notes/claude_token_usage.md` for how it is derived and what it
is worth.

## Querying — Tier 1

Named functions for the common questions. All take `family` first and `scope` as a keyword
(§ Scope below).

```python
from analysis.causal_graph import budget, tool_usage, goods, failed_tools, turns

budget(family, by="model")
# {'claude-fable-5': {'input_tokens': 46307, 'output_tokens': 159580,
#                     'cache_read_tokens': 10599998, 'cache_write_tokens': 506275,
#                     'estimated_reasoning_tokens': 67016}}
```

Reasoning was 67,016 of 159,580 output tokens here — 42% of everything the model produced.
`by` also takes `turn`, `assistant`, `subagent`.

#   'hunks': [{'start': 22, 'len': 15}], 'mime_type': None, 'remote_id': None}, ...]

failed_tools(family, n=3)    # {tool_name: {count, tools: [node]}} for count >= n
turns(family, status="interrupted")
```

## Querying — Tier 2

A JSON list of ops, run left to right, each op fed the previous result. This is what an LLM
composes for questions Tier 1 does not cover — no parser, no arbitrary code.

```python
from analysis.causal_graph import run_plan

run_plan(family, [
    {"op": "select",    "type": "tool"},
    {"op": "group_by",  "key": "tool_name"},
    {"op": "aggregate", "fn": "count"},

```

```python

    {"op": "group_by",  "key": "tool_name"},
    {"op": "filter",    "where": {"count": {">": 3}}},
    {"op": "aggregate", "fn": "collect", "key": "tool_result"},
], scope="tree")
```

The full op catalog is at the end of this file.

git commit -q -F - <<'MSG'
causal_graph: estimated reasoning tokens on the assistant node

Reasoning is billed inside output_tokens and never broken out. The normalizer
emits the ingredients (estimated_visible_tokens, tool_call_count); this turns
them into a number on the assistant node and rolls it up through budget.

    reasoning = output_tokens - ratio*sum(visible) - framing

Constants and their provenance: docs/design/notes/claude_token_usage.md.

Vendor-keyed config (config.py, config/causal_graph/reasoning.yaml). Every
constant was measured on Claude and none transfers: codex runs OpenAI models
where o200k_base IS the native tokenizer, so its ratio is exactly 1.0, and its
tool framing is a different unmeasured shape. for_vendor() returns a bare
zero-framing config for any vendor not declared -- it never falls through to
claude_code. An unmeasured model gets ratio 1.0, i.e. no conversion claimed,
which makes the estimate an upper bound rather than a confident wrong number.

Reported beats estimated: the branch is on reasoning_tokens being present, so
Codex needs no special case and a future Claude release needs no code change.

Node carries the answer, its provenance, and its ingredients:
    estimated_reasoning_tokens, reasoning_source, reasoning_ratio,
    estimated_visible_tokens, tool_call_count
The ingredients mean a ratio change is re-derivable from the graph alone rather
than needing a re-normalize; it takes effect on the next build or load, never
retroactively.

Rollup: estimated_reasoning_tokens joins TOKEN_FIELDS, so turn/assistant/
subagent/model budgets pick it up. It is deliberately NOT in ops'
_TOKEN_TOTAL_FIELDS -- it is billed inside output_tokens, so folding it into the
derived `tokens` scalar would double count.

Two correctness fixes found while doing this:

  * The budget cache was written into graph.meta/turn.meta and serialized by
    to_dict(), so a dumped graph carried stale aggregates. Invalidation keyed on
    node count alone, which a new TOKEN_FIELDS entry does not change -- a
    pre-change graph would have reloaded and silently served a budget with
    reasoning absent. to_dict() now strips it; the in-memory cache key includes
    the field set. Memoization kept, persistence gone.
  * builder read 25+ payload keys through .get(), so an upstream rename yielded
    None with no error and no failing test. _REQUIRED_PAYLOAD_FIELDS declares
    them and a test asserts each against the published normalized_schema.json.

README rewritten around usage: normalize -> build -> query, with the Family
object, a turn, a tool node and an assistant node, and real output for budget,
tool_usage, goods and two Tier-2 plans. Every value is from a live build of a
539-record session, not invented.

# Graph CLI: family-on-disk layout + build-all

## Context

The CLI works on files only, so it must be able to find a master's subagent graphs on disk.
Two things are in the way, one of them a live bug.

**Confirmed current behaviour** (read from source, and built against real data):

- **Build input is already fine.** A normalizer master file contains its subagents inline —
  `0f5e45b9-….json` holds 3 sessions (master + 2 children) — and `build_family` on that file
  alone resolves both spawns. No discovery needed on the way in.
- **Build output is flat and wrong for more than one session.** `_cmd_build` writes every graph
  as `out_dir/{session_id}.json`, master and subagents as siblings. `load_family` then globs
  `*.json` in that one directory, takes the first null-parent graph as master, and makes
  **everything else its children**:

  ```python
  graphs   = [load_graph(p) for p in sorted(out_dir.glob("*.json"))]
  masters  = [g for g in graphs if g.parent_session_id is None]
  children = {g.session_id: g for g in graphs if g is not master}
  ```

  Put two sessions in one `out_dir` and the second master and its subagents are silently
  adopted by the first. A warning is logged; nothing fails. That is exactly what `build-all`
  into a single directory would produce today, so the layout has to change first.

Grounded on `/Users/sumandra/projects/talium/traces/nrm_sess/`: 135 JSON files, subagents one
level deep only (no `subagents/*/subagents`), plus a `run_results.json` at the top that is not
an envelope.

## Ground rule 1 — family layout on disk

Mirror the layout Claude writes and the normalizer already reproduces:

```
<out_dir>/<project>/<master-session-id>.json
<out_dir>/<project>/<master-session-id>/subagents/<agent-id>.json
```

Owned by Python, not the shell.

- `store.py` gains `family_paths(root, master_id)` — the one place the layout is written down,
  so `dump` and `load` cannot disagree about it.
- `_cmd_build` writes the master at the top and each child under `<master-id>/subagents/`.
- `load_family` takes a **file** (the master graph envelope) and reads its children from
  `<master-stem>/subagents/*.json`. Directory input keeps working for a single-family dir so
  existing callers and tests do not break, but the file form is primary — "the CLI works on
  files".
- `_family_from_src` must now tell two file kinds apart: a *normalizer* envelope (has
  `sessions`) is built on the fly; a *graph* envelope (has `nodes`) is loaded with its family.
  Today it assumes any file is a normalizer envelope.

Descendants are flattened under the master's `subagents/`, not nested per parent. `Family` is
flat (`children: dict[session_id, Graph]`) and `parent_session_id` on each envelope preserves
the real tree, so nesting would add path depth without adding information. Real data is one
level deep anyway; the corpus has a grandchild, which is the case to test.

## Ground rule 2 — `build-all`

`utils/graph.sh build-all <src_dir> -o <out_dir>`, mirroring `test_normalizer.sh`:

- Walk `*.json` under `src_dir`, preserving each file's path relative to `src_dir` in `out_dir`
  (as `test_normalizer.sh` does with `rel="${jsonl#"$source_dir"/}"`). Keeps projects apart and
  avoids session-id collisions across them.
- **Skip any file under a `subagents/` path segment.** Those sessions are already inside their
  master's envelope; building them separately would emit duplicate orphan graphs. This is the
  selector that makes the command correct, and the thing most likely to be got wrong.
- **Skip files with no `sessions` key** — `run_results.json` sits in the corpus root and is not
  an envelope.
- Skip existing outputs unless `--force`, and write a `run_results.json` summary
  (built/skipped/error counts + per-file rows), same shape as the normalizer's.

Implemented as a subcommand in `cli_graph.py` with the shell wrapper only forwarding, so the
walk is testable. `utils/graph.sh` is a one-line `exec` today and should stay that way.

## Files

```
src/analysis/causal_graph/store.py       family_paths(); dump/load unchanged otherwise
src/analysis/causal_graph/cli_graph.py   load_family(file|dir), _cmd_build nesting,
                                         _cmd_build_all, _family_from_src discrimination
utils/graph.sh                           forward build-all (no logic)
tests/analysis/causal_graph/test_cli.py  layout + build-all cases
```

## Verification

- `pytest tests/ -q` green (1262 + new).
- **The bug this fixes, as a test:** build two different masters into one `out_dir`, load each
  by file, assert each family has only its own children. This fails on today's code.
- Round trip: build → load-by-file → same node count and same child session ids as
  `build_family` produced directly from the normalizer envelope.
- Grandchild case: the corpus has `agent-grandchild-1` under `agent-sonnet-1`; assert it lands
  in the master's `subagents/` and still resolves.
- End to end on real data:
  `utils/graph.sh build-all /Users/sumandra/projects/talium/traces/nrm_sess -o /tmp/graphs`,
  then confirm the master count equals the number of non-`subagents/` envelopes, that
  `run_results.json` reports zero errors, and that loading one master by file yields the same
  children as its normalized source.

## Note, not part of this item

`traces/nrm_sess` still predates the `estimated_visible_tokens` rename, so graphs built from it
carry no reasoning estimate. Structure work here is unaffected; re-normalize before trusting
any reasoning number out of it.

# --- build-all -------------------------------------------------------------------------


def _write_envelope(path: Path, master_id: str) -> None:
    """A normalizer envelope with `master_id` and one subagent, at `path`."""
    env = json.loads(json.dumps(_envelope()))
    for session in env["sessions"]:
        if session["parent_session_id"] is None:
            session["session_id"] = master_id
        else:
            session["session_id"] = f"{master_id}-child"
            session["parent_session_id"] = master_id
    path.parent.mkdir(parents=True, exist_ok=True)
    path.write_text(json.dumps(env), encoding="utf-8")


def test_build_all_mirrors_the_source_tree(tmp_path, capsys):
    src = tmp_path / "nrm"
    _write_envelope(src / "projA" / "s1.json", "s1")
    _write_envelope(src / "projB" / "s2.json", "s2")
    out = tmp_path / "graphs"

    cli_graph.main(["build-all", str(src), "-o", str(out)])

    # projects stay apart, so session ids cannot collide across them
    assert (out / "projA" / "s1.json").is_file()
    assert (out / "projA" / "s1" / "subagents" / "s1-child.json").is_file()
    assert (out / "projB" / "s2.json").is_file()

    summary = _last_stdout_json(capsys)
    assert summary["counts"] == {"built": 2, "skipped": 0, "error": 0}


def test_build_all_ignores_envelopes_under_subagents(tmp_path, capsys):
    """The selector that makes the command correct.

    The normalizer writes each subagent BOTH inline in its master's envelope and as its own
    file under `<session>/subagents/`. Building those files again would emit orphan graphs
    whose spawns resolve to nothing and whose tokens double-count in any cross-session rollup.
    """
    src = tmp_path / "nrm"
    _write_envelope(src / "proj" / "s1.json", "s1")
    _write_envelope(src / "proj" / "s1" / "subagents" / "agent-x.json", "agent-x")
    out = tmp_path / "graphs"

    cli_graph.main(["build-all", str(src), "-o", str(out)])

    summary = _last_stdout_json(capsys)
    assert summary["counts"]["built"] == 1, "a subagent envelope was built as its own family"
    assert not (out / "proj" / "s1" / "subagents" / "agent-x").exists()


def test_build_all_skips_non_envelopes(tmp_path, capsys):
    """`run_results.json` sits in the corpus root and is not an envelope.

    Skipped by shape (no `sessions` key), so no filename convention has to be maintained.
    """
    src = tmp_path / "nrm"
    _write_envelope(src / "proj" / "s1.json", "s1")
    (src / "run_results.json").write_text(json.dumps({"counts": {}}), encoding="utf-8")
    out = tmp_path / "graphs"

    cli_graph.main(["build-all", str(src), "-o", str(out)])

    summary = _last_stdout_json(capsys)
    assert summary["counts"] == {"built": 1, "skipped": 1, "error": 0}


def test_build_all_records_a_run_summary(tmp_path, capsys):
    src = tmp_path / "nrm"
    _write_envelope(src / "proj" / "s1.json", "s1")
    out = tmp_path / "graphs"
    cli_graph.main(["build-all", str(src), "-o", str(out)])
    capsys.readouterr()

    results = json.loads((out / "run_results.json").read_text(encoding="utf-8"))
    assert results["counts"]["built"] == 1
    row = next(r for r in results["files"] if r["status"] == "built")
    assert row["master"] == "s1" and row["children"] == 1 and row["nodes"] > 0
    assert row["out"] == str(Path("proj") / "s1.json")


def test_build_all_survives_one_bad_file(tmp_path, capsys):
    """One unreadable session must not abandon the rest of the batch."""
    src = tmp_path / "nrm"
    _write_envelope(src / "proj" / "s1.json", "s1")

git commit -q -F - <<'MSG'
graph CLI: family layout on disk, build-all, run report

The CLI works on files, so a master must be able to find its own subagents.

Layout. A family is a master envelope beside a directory named for it, mirroring
what Claude writes and the normalizer reproduces:

    <out>/<project>/<master-id>.json
    <out>/<project>/<master-id>/subagents/<child-id>.json

store.family_paths() is the single definition; writer and reader both call it, so
a dump and a load cannot drift apart.

This fixes a live bug. _cmd_build wrote every graph flat as <session_id>.json and
load_family globbed one directory, took the first null-parent graph as master and
adopted EVERY other file as its child. Two sessions in one directory meant the
second master and its subagents were silently attributed to the first, corrupting
any rollup computed from it -- a warning was logged, nothing failed. That is
exactly what build-all into one directory would have produced. A directory load
holding more than one master is now an error rather than a guess.

load_family takes a master file and reads children from the subagents/ dir beside
it; the directory form stays for single-family stores. _family_from_src now tells
a graph envelope (nodes) from a normalizer envelope (sessions) by content rather
than by extension, since both end in .json.

build-all recurses a source tree, mirrors it into the output so projects stay
apart and session ids cannot collide, and continues past a bad file instead of
abandoning the batch. Two exclusions carry the correctness:

  * anything under a subagents/ directory -- the normalizer writes each subagent
    both inline in its master's envelope and as its own file, so building those
    again emits orphan graphs whose spawns resolve to nothing and whose tokens
    double-count in a cross-session rollup;
  * files with no `sessions` key -- run_results.json shares the corpus root.
    Skipped by shape, so no filename convention has to be maintained.

Run report at <out>/run_results.json, field-for-field the normalizer's contract
(generated_at, source, target, total, counts, files[] keyed input/output/status/
message) so both batch tools are read and diffed the same way, plus graph totals
(masters, subagents, nodes). Error rows carry the reason: a count says something
failed, only the message says what. Non-zero exit if anything errored.

Real corpus: 10 built, 1 skipped, 0 errors -- 10 masters, 62 subagents, 4852
nodes, against 10 source envelopes not under subagents/. Round trip verified:
loading a persisted master yields the same children and node count as building
from the normalized source directly.
