# Causal graph: usable interfaces — scope, examples, generated docs

## Context

The module has capability nobody can reach. `--scope subagent` returned zeros instead of an
error; the Tier-2 op catalog lists eleven ops of which only four appear in any example; the
seven that carry the real power (`attr`, `children`, `parent`, `neighbors`, `descendants`,
`path`, `resolve`) have none, and their edge variants (`contain`/`loop`/`spawn`, `up`/`down`)
are invisible. These are interfaces people will build sophisticated queries on, and they do not
explain themselves.

Decisions taken:

- **scope values are `self` | `tree` | `subagents` | `<session-id>`.** Plural `subagents`
  (all children, master excluded) so it cannot be confused with `--arg by=subagent`, which
  groups results per child and is a different thing.
- **`.graph/` is committed** as `examples/causal_graph/graphs/`, so every example is
  reproducible by anyone who clones.
- **Repo-root `examples/<module>/` is the convention** from now on; `src/common/msging/examples/`
  stays where it is (it is an importable package loaded by `tests/common/msging/test_examples.py`
  and referenced from its README — moving it is churn for no gain). Written into CLAUDE.md, which
  currently says nothing about examples.
- **A plan file carries its own `description`**, so adding an example is one file and the README
  follows.

## 1. Scope semantics

`family.graphs_in_scope` gains `subagents` -> `list(family.children.values())`.

**An unrecognised scope raises**, naming the valid values and the family's actual child ids.
Today it returns `[]`, which is why `--scope subagent` reported zeros rather than a mistake.
The legitimate partial-family case still returns empty: a scope naming a child the master
genuinely spawned but which is not loaded is a real state, distinguishable from a typo via the
spawn nodes' `refs.child_session_id`.

**Collapse the two resolvers.** `ops.py::_Ctx._graphs_in_scope` is a second implementation of
the same contract and has already diverged — it raises `OpError` where `family.graphs_in_scope`
returns `[]`, which is exactly why the same bad scope errored through a Tier-2 plan and silently
zeroed through `budget`. `ops` delegates to `family`; the duplicate goes.

## 2. Sample graphs

Move `.graph/` -> `examples/causal_graph/graphs/` (3.9 MB, 73 files, 10 masters).

**Scan before committing.** `redaction_patterns` defaults to an empty list, so no secret-pattern
scrub ever ran on these — only the generated-content scrub (verified: all 559 Write/Edit inputs
carry `[CONTENT OMITTED]`). What is unscrubbed is 278 full `user_prompt.text` values and 2,069
tool inputs (Bash commands, absolute paths). Scan both for token-shaped strings before the
files enter history, which is permanent. Report anything found rather than silently scrubbing.

Also generate `examples/causal_graph/graphs-fixture/` from the committed corpus — small,
deterministic, no real content — as the fast target for tests.

## 3. Plan files

`examples/causal_graph/plans/<name>.json`:

```json
{ "description": "Which tool most often runs right before an error?",
  "plan": [ {"op": "select", "type": "tool", "where": {"is_error": true}}, ... ] }
```

`cli_graph._cmd_query` accepts either this shape or a bare list, so nothing existing breaks.

The set, chosen to cover the ops with no example rather than to demonstrate syntax:

```
repeated_tools.json           same tool+input recurring        select -> group_by -> filter
tool_before_error.json        what runs just before a failure  neighbors edge=loop dir=prev
turns_touching_markdown.json  turns that touched a .md file    descendants edge=contain dir=up
subagent_work.json            what delegated work produced     neighbors edge=spawn -> resolve
tools_under_a_turn.json       containment, both directions     children / parent
path_between.json             how two nodes connect            path (BFS)
reasoning_hotspots.json       where reasoning tokens went      select -> attr -> aggregate
```

Every one is verified against the committed graphs before it ships. A plan that does not run is
worse than no example.

## 4. `examples/causal_graph/README.md`

Structure as specified: what this is; folder layout and how to run; Tier-1 worked examples;
Tier-2 detail.

**Both example sections are generated** by `utils/gen_graph_interface.py`, which already owns
the `<!-- gen:… -->` block machinery and is already pinned by `tests/utils/test_doc_generators.py`
— a second target file is less machinery than a second script plus new CI wiring.

- Tier-2 section walks `plans/*.json`, runs each against the committed graphs, and renders
  description, plan, shell command, real output. **Add a plan, regenerate, done.** `--check`
  fails if someone adds one and forgets.
- Tier-1 section covers what the module README omits: `failed_tools`, `turns`, `loops`, and
  scope in action (`self` vs `tree` vs `subagents` on the same query), since that is what caused
  the confusion.
- Also a Python file showing the in-process API, because `resolve` returns a `Graph` object that
  the CLI flattens to JSON and loses.

## 5. Module README + convention

- Generated usage block gains the missing `user_prompt` and `spawn` node examples (it shows
  `turn`, `tool`, `assistant` only).
- CLAUDE.md: repo-root `examples/<module>/`, examples must run in CI, msging grandfathered.

## 6. Not in this batch

`causal_graph_schema.json` descriptions — the long-open item. Same theme, but it is a published
contract with its own version and drift guard, and bundling a contract change with a docs change
makes both harder to review and to revert. **Separate commit, immediately after this one.**

## Verification

- `pytest tests/ -q` green (1279 + new).
- Every plan runs clean against both graph sets; a test executes all of them so a broken example
  fails CI.
- Scope: `subagents` returns children only; master tokens absent from the result. Unknown scope
  raises naming valid values. A spawned-but-unloaded child still returns empty, not an error.
  Assert Tier-1 and Tier-2 now agree on the same bad scope — the divergence being fixed.
- `gen_graph_interface.py --check` clean; adding a plan file without regenerating fails it.
- Secret scan output reported before the graphs are committed.

old = '''def graphs_in_scope(family: Family, scope: str = "tree") -> list[Graph]:
    """The graphs a query touches under ``scope`` (design §3.2).

    ``self`` -> master only; ``tree`` (DEFAULT) -> master + all descendants; any other value
    is a subagent session-id -> just that one graph (empty list if it is not in the family,
    consistent with the partial-family contract).
    """

new = '''SCOPE_KEYWORDS = ("self", "tree", "subagents")


def _spawned_session_ids(family: Family) -> set[str]:
    """Every child session id the family's spawn nodes reference, loaded or not.

    The discriminator between "a subagent that exists but is not loaded" and "a typo": the
    first is a real state under the partial-family contract, the second is a mistake, and
    returning an empty result for both is what made a bad scope look like a real answer.
    """
    return {
        ref
        for graph in family.all_graphs()
        for node in graph.nodes.values()
        if (ref := node.refs.get("child_session_id"))
    }


def graphs_in_scope(family: Family, scope: str = "tree") -> list[Graph]:
    """The graphs a query touches under ``scope`` (design §3.2).

    ```
    self          master only
    tree          master + all descendants          (DEFAULT)
    subagents     descendants only, master excluded
    <session-id>  one named child
    ```

    ``subagents`` is plural on purpose: ``budget``'s ``by="subagent"`` groups results *per*
    child and is a different thing, so the two must not share a spelling.

    Raises ``ValueError`` for a scope that is neither a keyword nor a session the family knows
    about. It used to return ``[]``, which reported a typo as a legitimate empty answer --
    ``--scope subagent`` (singular) came back as zero tokens rather than a mistake.
    """
    if scope == "self":
        return [family.master]
    if scope == "tree":
        return family.all_graphs()
    if scope == "subagents":
        return list(family.children.values())

    graph = family.resolve(scope)
    if graph is not None:
        return [graph]
    if scope in _spawned_session_ids(family):
        # Spawned but not loaded: a partial family (OTEL-live, or a child not yet built).
        # Empty is the honest answer here and the caller reports `partial` (design §3.2).
        return []

    known = sorted(family.children)
    raise ValueError(
        f"unknown scope {scope!r}. Expected one of {', '.join(SCOPE_KEYWORDS)}, "
        f"or a subagent session id: {', '.join(known) if known else '(this family has none)'}"
    )'''

open(p, 'w').write(s.replace(old, new))

input.subject: Add a `sort` op to the Tier-2 catalog
input.description:
Ordering is not expressible in a plan. `select` happens to return timestamp order (verified: all 33 spawns ts-sorted at self and tree scope) but only because the builder inserts turn by turn and select iterates insertion order — nothing guarantees it, and a change to graph assembly would silently reorder results. There is an internal structural DFS order (_Ctx.order) but it serves the `loop` edge and is unreachable from a plan. Proposal: {"op": "sort", "key": "ts", "desc": false} reading through get_attr, so it works on derived fields and files[]. paths for free. Also unlocks "top N by X", currently impossible — aggregate max returns the value, not the ranked list.</description>

input.subject: Add parent_id to the node so the tree can be walked
input.description:
A dumped node carries `children` (down) but no parent, so a row cannot say which turn it belongs to and `select turn -> children` flattens 315 nodes losing all linkage. Blocks time-ordered walks and any per-turn rollup. Verified the immediate use case (cache hit ratio over time) already works via `select type=assistant` now that nodes render whole — 263 rows with all token fields, ts-ordered. Proposal: add parent_id to the Node model, set by the builder. Gives (id, parent_id, ts, attrs) adjacency-list form; consumer groups by parent_id. One field, benefits every query, no new result type. Alternative considered: a `walk` op emitting {level, parent, attrs} rows — more expressive but introduces a second result kind every downstream op must handle. Schema change either way, so it needs a SCHEMA_VERSION bump.</description>

input.subject: Roll up token usage onto the turn node at build time
input.description:
`select type=turn` returns only prompt_id/status/duration_ms — token totals need a second `budget(by=turn)` call plus a join to get ts alongside. Proposal: compute at build, store as a NESTED turn.attrs.tokens object (not flat siblings) so it cannot be confused with an assistant's own usage and summed twice — same trap class as estimated_reasoning_tokens being inside output_tokens. Cost measured: 1.3ms for the whole corpus (9 families, 3674 nodes, 190 turns), 0.14ms per family. Precedent: duration_ms is ALREADY a whole-turn rollup on the same node, so this is not a new kind of field. Two things to settle: (a) containment-only sum vs including subagents spawned in the turn — budget(by=turn) does the latter via the spawn edge; recommend storing containment-only and documenting it, since it is well-defined without a loaded family; (b) OTEL append (update()) makes a stored rollup stale, so build it as a per-turn function that can be re-run, not a one-shot at load. NOTE: contradicts "Structure only; the graph never aggregates" stated in causal-graph-design.md lines 25 and 435 and README line 10 — the design doc must be updated in the same change, not silently diverged from.</description>

git commit -q -F - <<'MSG'
causal_graph: usable interfaces — scope, examples, self-explaining contract

Executes docs/plan/2026-08-21-causal-graph-usability.md. The module had
capability nobody could reach: `--scope subagent` returned zeros instead of an
error, seven of eleven Tier-2 ops had no example, and the published schema said
`attrs: "dict"`.

Scope. Adds `subagents` (children only, master excluded) — plural so it cannot
be confused with `--arg by=subagent`, which groups per child. An unrecognised
scope now RAISES naming the valid values; it used to return [], which is why a
singular typo reported zero tokens rather than a mistake. A child the master
genuinely spawned but which is not loaded still returns empty — that is the
partial-family contract, told apart via spawn refs. Collapses the two scope
resolvers: ops.py had a second implementation that raised where family.py
returned [], so the same bad scope errored through Tier-2 and silently zeroed
through budget.

Sample corpus. 10 real sessions, 62 subagents, 73 files under
examples/causal_graph/graphs/, so every documented output reproduces on a clean
clone. Scanned before committing: 2,069 tool inputs and 278 prompts against 12
credential patterns, no hits; generated file content was already scrubbed
([CONTENT OMITTED] on all 559 Write/Edit).

Examples. examples/<module>/ is now the repo-wide convention (CLAUDE.md;
msging's stays put, it is an importable package). Eight plans, each a
{description, plan} file so adding one is a single edit — the README's Tier-2
section is generated by walking plans/. test_examples.py runs every one in CI
and asserts none returns an empty result.

Contract. causal_graph_schema.json gains per-node-type attrs shapes derived from
the real graphs, each field carrying prose from one authored source
(descriptions.py). The generator refuses to write an undocumented field.

Output. Nodes render whole rather than as ids — an id-only answer forces a
lookup and there is no lookup command. A Graph from resolve stays an id, since
inlining a session would bury the result. Node lists come back in time order as
a guarantee: select already did, but only because the builder inserts turn by
turn, and a change to assembly would have reordered everything silently.

parent_id on every node, derived in one pass from children so the two directions
cannot disagree. Turns carry a nested attrs.tokens rollup of the assistants
beneath them — containment-only, excluding subagents, which is a different
number from budget(by=turn) and differs on exactly the 2 of 52 turns that
spawned. Nested, not flat, so it cannot be summed with a leaf's own usage.
Together these remove both joins: usage-by-turn and group-by-turn are each one
call now. Graph SCHEMA_VERSION 1.0.0 -> 2.0.0.

Removes `path`. Containment is three levels deep (279/2,380/2,193 nodes, none
below), so its answer was always one determined route of at most five nodes; it
could not cross the spawn edge, which is where the causal question lives; and
everything it did is `descendants dir=up` plus a filter, which works across
scopes. A plan naming it now raises rather than returning [].

Two things found while writing the examples, both fixed: file attributes were
unreachable (`extension` lives under attrs.files[], so a top-level where matched
none of 347 nodes and the design's own §5.3 example returned nothing — now
addressable as files[].extension), and quiet_logs() leaked structlog's
process-wide config out of a module fixture and broke 22 msging tests.

Design doc updated rather than left to diverge: "the graph never aggregates" was
already false when written, since duration_ms has always been a whole-turn
rollup. The line is now drawn at build-time-derivable-from-containment.

input.plan:
# Normalizer: line counts, and structured result facts

**First action after approval:** write this to
`docs/plan/2026-08-22-normalizer-tool-result-facts.md`. Plan mode cannot write outside the
plan file.

Two changes, deliberately separate: one fixes a derivation that never worked, one adds a
mechanism. Each reviewable and revertable alone.

## Context

Tool result content is scrubbed unconditionally — the rule set at the start of this work, and
it stays. But blanket-dropping lost facts that are not content: a commit sha is evidence of
what a session produced, not a copy of anything.

Measured across the raw corpus (146 files):

```
gitOperation      89   Bash only    dict, 30-100 bytes, ALREADY STRUCTURED
totalDurationMs  116   Agent only   int
structuredPatch 1690   Write/Edit   list, up to 58 KB  <- content, never promoted
linesAdded         0   Write/Edit   ABSENT. the field the normalizer reads does not exist
```

`gitOperation` appears only on git operations that produce something durable — `commit`,
`push`, `pr`, `branch`. `git status`/`log`/`diff`/`show` (145/96/62/44 calls) carry no flag, so
`git diff` output is excluded by the vendor's own distinction rather than a rule we maintain.

Two things were checked and **rejected**:

- **`totalTokens` / `usage`** — despite the name, `usage.iterations` holds a single entry and
  `totalTokens` is that one message's field sum. Against derived child-graph totals it is
  15-18x low (58,100 vs 1,052,907 on one subagent). Promoting it would place a field called
  `totalTokens` beside our own, disagreeing wildly, with nothing explaining which is right.
- **`toolStats.linesAdded`** — Agent-only and per-run, so it covers delegated work and nothing
  else, at a coarser grain than change 1 produces. Redundant once line counts are derived.

# Normalizer: hunks, structured result facts, config-first

**First action after approval:** write this to
`docs/plan/2026-08-22-normalizer-tool-result-facts.md`. Plan mode cannot write outside the
plan file.

Three changes, deliberately separate and each reviewable alone:

1. **remove** two fields that have never held a value, and complete the hunks
2. **add** a promotion bag for vendor-structured facts the blanket scrub was discarding
3. **fix** the one service whose config file is not what actually runs

The thread joining them: the unconditional tool-result scrub was right about content and wrong
about facts. Nothing here relaxes it — no result text reaches a payload in any of the three.

## Context

Tool result content is scrubbed unconditionally — the rule set at the start of this work, and
it stays. But blanket-dropping lost facts that are not content: a commit sha is evidence of
what a session produced, not a copy of anything.

Measured across the raw corpus (146 files):

```
gitOperation      89   Bash only    dict, 30-100 bytes, ALREADY STRUCTURED
totalDurationMs  116   Agent only   int
structuredPatch 1690   Write/Edit   list, up to 58 KB  <- content, never promoted
linesAdded         0   Write/Edit   ABSENT. the field the normalizer reads does not exist
```

`gitOperation` appears only on git operations that produce something durable — `commit`,
`push`, `pr`, `branch`. `git status`/`log`/`diff`/`show` (145/96/62/44 calls) carry no flag, so
`git diff` output is excluded by the vendor's own distinction rather than a rule we maintain.

Two things were checked and **rejected**:

- **`totalTokens` / `usage`** — despite the name, `usage.iterations` holds a single entry and
  `totalTokens` is that one message's field sum. Against derived child-graph totals it is
  15-18x low (58,100 vs 1,052,907 on one subagent). Promoting it would place a field called
  `totalTokens` beside our own, disagreeing wildly, with nothing explaining which is right.
- **`toolStats.linesAdded`** — Agent-only and per-run, so it covers delegated work and nothing
  else, at a coarser grain than change 1 produces. Redundant once line counts are derived.

## Change 1 — remove the dead line-count fields

`claude_code.py:1221` reads `tool_use_result["linesAdded"]`. That key is **absent on all 1,690
Edit/Write results** — it exists only inside `toolStats`, which is Agent-only. So
`lines_added` / `lines_removed` have always been null on every file the pipeline has ever seen.

**Remove them from the contract**, on `file_change` and on `tool_call.files[]`. A permanently
null field is worse than an absent one: it reads as "this edit added no lines" rather than "we
do not know". Drop the dead reads with them.

**Keep the hunks, and add `old_len`.** `_hunks_from_structured_patch` (line 185) currently keeps
`{start: newStart, len: newLines}` and discards `oldLines`, so how much an edit *moved* is not
recoverable from stored data. One extra field in a function already running makes net delta
computable by a consumer — first access, distilled downstream.

Not doing: counting `+`/`-` prefixes in `lines[]` to synthesise added/removed. That is a
different mechanism (derive-a-scalar-from-content) and not wanted here.

## Change 2 — a promotion bag for vendor-structured facts

New payload field on `tool_result`, merged onto the graph's tool node the way `is_error` already
is:

```json5
"result": {                                   // absent when nothing was promoted
  "git_operation": {"commit": {"sha": "75d8bc9", "kind": "committed"}},
  "agent_duration_ms": 463387
}
```

`is_error` / `tool_denial_kind` stay flat — universal outcome fields every tool has. The bag
holds *tool-specific* structured facts. State that distinction, or the two look arbitrary.

**Config-driven allowlist**, mirroring the existing `usage_field_map` (`config.py:84`) so a new
key is a config line, never code. Lands in `config/normalizer/claude_code.yaml`, beside it:

```yaml
tool_result_field_map:
  gitOperation:    git_operation       # Bash: commit/push/pr/branch, <=100 bytes
  totalDurationMs: agent_duration_ms   # Agent: wall-clock for a delegation
```

## Change 3 — the config file is what runs

`cli_normalize.py:103` has `--config default=None`, so the YAML is read only when passed and
every real run has used the built-in Python defaults. It is the only service that does this:

```
uploader / ingest / worker / storage   --config default="config/<svc>.yaml"
collect                                --config required=True
normalize                              --config default=None      <- the outlier
```

Bring it in line: `--config` defaults to `config/normalizer/claude_code.yaml`, and the shipped
file states **every** value explicitly so a run is fully described by a file on disk.

Pydantic defaults stay as the model's declared schema — 37 sites construct `NormalizerConfig(...)`
directly, nearly all tests passing one kwarg to exercise one behaviour, and a text-cap test
should not need a YAML file. To stop the two drifting: **a guard test asserting the shipped
config loads to exactly `NormalizerConfig()`**. Same mechanism as every other contract here — if
someone changes a default in code and not the file, it fails.

Seam, named not built: a later split of user-facing config from internal dev properties, so the
former cannot tread on the latter.

**Three rules that keep the bag from becoming a content channel**, all enforced in code:

- promote only values the vendor already structured — **never** text parsed out of `stdout`;
- reject bare strings above a small cap, and cap the serialized bag;
- a key is added only after checking *what it measures*. `totalTokens` is the cautionary case:
  the name said one thing, the arithmetic said another. Put that in the config comment, since
  the point of the allowlist is that someone extends it later without this conversation.

Deliberately not included, revisit when samples exist: API/MCP response status.

## Files

```
src/collector/normalizer/claude_code.py   _hunks_from_structured_patch (185);
                                          the enrich site (1214-1240); _make_tool_result (1059)
src/collector/normalizer/config.py        tool_result_field_map, beside usage_field_map
src/common/events/descriptions.py         prose for `result` and the corrected line counts
src/common/events/normalized_schema.json  REGENERATED
src/analysis/causal_graph/builder.py       merge `result` onto the tool node (change 2)
src/analysis/causal_graph/descriptions.py  `result` on the tool node
docs/modules/normalizer.md                 the two mechanisms, and why they differ
```

## Verification

| | |
|---|---|
| lines | `lines_added`/`lines_removed` gone from the schema, and from the graph's `files[]` |
| lines | `old_len` present per hunk; `len - old_len` reproduces the net delta on a checked hunk |
| bag | `git_operation` present on 89 Bash results, absent on `git diff`/`log`/`status`/`show` |
| bag | `agent_duration_ms` present on 116 Agent results only |
| bag | a config entry naming a large key (`stdout`, `file`) is rejected, not truncated |
| bag | `result` absent, not empty, when nothing was promoted |
| config | a run with no `--config` reads the YAML — assert via `meta_info.config_digest` |
| config | the shipped YAML loads to exactly `NormalizerConfig()`; changing one and not the other fails |
| safety | no result text reaches any payload — existing leak probes stay clean |
| contract | schema republished; `pytest tests/ -q` green (1315 baseline) |

Removing `lines_added`/`lines_removed` is a field removal, so `SCHEMA_VERSION` takes a **major**
bump by the rules in `src/common/events/__init__.py` — not the minor I first assumed. The bag
and `old_len` are additive.

The graph side rides along: `builder.py` reads `files[].lines_added`, and its
`descriptions.py` documents both fields. Both need updating in the same change or the drift
guard fails.

what a session produced, not a copy of anything.

Measured across the raw corpus (146 files):

```
gitOperation      89   Bash only    dict, 30-100 bytes, ALREADY STRUCTURED
totalDurationMs  116   Agent only   int
structuredPatch 1690   Write/Edit   list, up to 58 KB  <- content, never promoted
linesAdded         0   Write/Edit   ABSENT. the field the normalizer reads does not exist
```

`gitOperation` appears only on git operations that produce something durable — `commit`,
`push`, `pr`, `branch`. `git status`/`log`/`diff`/`show` (145/96/62/44 calls) carry no flag, so
`git diff` output is excluded by the vendor's own distinction rather than a rule we maintain.

Two things were checked and **rejected**:

- **`totalTokens` / `usage`** — despite the name, `usage.iterations` holds a single entry and
  `totalTokens` is that one message's field sum. Against derived child-graph totals it is
  15-18x low (58,100 vs 1,052,907 on one subagent). Promoting it would place a field called
  `totalTokens` beside our own, disagreeing wildly, with nothing explaining which is right.
- **`toolStats.linesAdded`** — Agent-only and per-run, so it covers delegated work and nothing
  else, at a coarser grain than change 1 produces. Redundant once line counts are derived.

## Change 1 — remove the dead line-count fields

`claude_code.py:1221` reads `tool_use_result["linesAdded"]`. That key is **absent on all 1,690
Edit/Write results** — it exists only inside `toolStats`, which is Agent-only. So
`lines_added` / `lines_removed` have always been null on every file the pipeline has ever seen.

**Remove them from the contract**, on `file_change` and on `tool_call.files[]`. A permanently
null field is worse than an absent one: it reads as "this edit added no lines" rather than "we
do not know". Drop the dead reads with them.

**Keep the hunks, and add `old_len`.** `_hunks_from_structured_patch` (line 185) currently keeps
`{start: newStart, len: newLines}` and discards `oldLines`, so how much an edit *moved* is not
recoverable from stored data. One extra field in a function already running makes net delta
computable by a consumer — first access, distilled downstream.

Not doing: counting `+`/`-` prefixes in `lines[]` to synthesise added/removed. That is a
different mechanism (derive-a-scalar-from-content) and not wanted here.

## Change 2 — a promotion bag for vendor-structured facts

New payload field on `tool_result`, merged onto the graph's tool node the way `is_error` already
is:

```json5
"result": {                                   // absent when nothing was promoted
  "git_operation": {"commit": {"sha": "75d8bc9", "kind": "committed"}},
  "agent_duration_ms": 463387
}
```

`is_error` / `tool_denial_kind` stay flat — universal outcome fields every tool has. The bag
holds *tool-specific* structured facts. State that distinction, or the two look arbitrary.

**Config-driven allowlist**, mirroring the existing `usage_field_map` (`config.py:84`) so a new
key is a config line, never code. Lands in `config/normalizer/claude_code.yaml`, beside it:

```yaml
tool_result_field_map:
  gitOperation:    git_operation       # Bash: commit/push/pr/branch, <=100 bytes
  totalDurationMs: agent_duration_ms   # Agent: wall-clock for a delegation
```

## Change 3 — the config file is what runs

`cli_normalize.py:103` has `--config default=None`, so the YAML is read only when passed and
every real run has used the built-in Python defaults. It is the only service that does this:

```
uploader / ingest / worker / storage   --config default="config/<svc>.yaml"
collect                                --config required=True
normalize                              --config default=None      <- the outlier
```

Bring it in line: `--config` defaults to `config/normalizer/claude_code.yaml`, and the shipped
file states **every** value explicitly so a run is fully described by a file on disk.

Pydantic defaults stay as the model's declared schema — 37 sites construct `NormalizerConfig(...)`
directly, nearly all tests passing one kwarg to exercise one behaviour, and a text-cap test
should not need a YAML file. To stop the two drifting: **a guard test asserting the shipped
config loads to exactly `NormalizerConfig()`**. Same mechanism as every other contract here — if
someone changes a default in code and not the file, it fails.

Seam, named not built: a later split of user-facing config from internal dev properties, so the
former cannot tread on the latter.

**Three rules that keep the bag from becoming a content channel**, all enforced in code:

- promote only values the vendor already structured — **never** text parsed out of `stdout`;
- reject bare strings above a small cap, and cap the serialized bag;
- a key is added only after checking *what it measures*. `totalTokens` is the cautionary case:
  the name said one thing, the arithmetic said another. Put that in the config comment, since
  the point of the allowlist is that someone extends it later without this conversation.

Deliberately not included, revisit when samples exist: API/MCP response status.

## Files

```
src/collector/normalizer/claude_code.py   _hunks_from_structured_patch (185);
                                          the enrich site (1214-1240); _make_tool_result (1059)
src/collector/normalizer/config.py        tool_result_field_map, beside usage_field_map
src/common/events/descriptions.py         prose for `result` and the corrected line counts
src/common/events/normalized_schema.json  REGENERATED
src/analysis/causal_graph/builder.py       merge `result` onto the tool node (change 2)
src/analysis/causal_graph/descriptions.py  `result` on the tool node
docs/modules/normalizer.md                 the two mechanisms, and why they differ
```

## Verification

| | |
|---|---|
| lines | `lines_added`/`lines_removed` gone from the schema, and from the graph's `files[]` |
| lines | `old_len` present per hunk; `len - old_len` reproduces the net delta on a checked hunk |
| bag | `git_operation` present on 89 Bash results, absent on `git diff`/`log`/`status`/`show` |
| bag | `agent_duration_ms` present on 116 Agent results only |
| bag | a config entry naming a large key (`stdout`, `file`) is rejected, not truncated |
| bag | `result` absent, not empty, when nothing was promoted |
| config | a run with no `--config` reads the YAML — assert via `meta_info.config_digest` |
| config | the shipped YAML loads to exactly `NormalizerConfig()`; changing one and not the other fails |
| safety | no result text reaches any payload — existing leak probes stay clean |
| contract | schema republished; `pytest tests/ -q` green (1315 baseline) |

Removing `lines_added`/`lines_removed` is a field removal, so `SCHEMA_VERSION` takes a **major**
bump by the rules in `src/common/events/__init__.py` — not the minor I first assumed. The bag
and `old_len` are additive.

The graph side rides along: `builder.py` reads `files[].lines_added`, and its
`descriptions.py` documents both fields. Both need updating in the same change or the drift
guard fails.

    out = ""
    if comment:

    out += yaml.safe_dump({key: d[key]}, sort_keys=False, width=96, default_flow_style=False)

# nobody looked at. Every value the normalizer has is stated here, so a run is fully described
# by a file on disk.
#
# The pydantic model (src/collector/normalizer/config.py) still declares defaults, because
# tests construct NormalizerConfig(...) directly to exercise one behaviour at a time. The two

    "  2. it must be small. max_result_value_bytes rejects the rest rather than truncating,\n"
    "     because a truncated fact is a wrong fact.\n"
    "  3. add a key only after checking WHAT IT MEASURES. `totalTokens` is the cautionary\n"
    "     case: the name says a subagent's run total, the arithmetic says one message's field\n"
